title: Brain training
paragraphs: Our brain is probably the most important organ in our body. It's an incredibly complex thing that helps us think, speak, feel and move. It's no wonder we need to look after it and just like the rest of our body, we need to keep it exercised to keep it healthy.

Our brain is made up of 86 billion neurons - or nerve cells - but as we get older some of these slowly die off. In extreme cases, nerve cells in different areas of the brain become damaged and eventually die causing a condition called dementia where a person is unable to perform certain mental functions.

It's a good idea to train our brain by learning ways to increase our memory or intelligence. I like to stretch my brain by doing a crossword or a Sudoku puzzle. There's also evidence that learning a second language can boost your brainpower. Dr Catherine Loveday, who's a neuropsychologist, thinks being bilingual is a protective factor for the brain because it "involves a lot of switchings and that seems to exercise the sort of executive parts of our brain. Those parts of the brain are kind of stronger and fitter when it comes to resisting some kind of damage from a stroke."

The main aim of trying these skills is to stimulate the brain. This is something Dr. Loveday describes as building up our cognitive reserve - that's building up extra abilities to help protect the brain against declining memory or thinking. She says "even if people take up languages or take up other things later in life it will give them a degree of protection." As I get older, that has put my mind at rest!

The best bit of research I have read is that eating chocolate may enhance our ability to acquire and utilise knowledge - that's our cognitive performance. It may not be healthy for the rest of my body but at least it might make me a brain box! What do you think?

vocabulary.example: The heart is a vital organ in the human body.
vocabulary.translation: 心脏是人体中至关重要的器官。

vocabulary.example: Neurons transmit information throughout the nervous system.
vocabulary.translation: 神经元在整个神经系统中传递信息。

vocabulary.entry: die off [phr.] /daɪ ɒf/ 相继死亡 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The bees in the hive are dying off due to disease.
vocabulary.translation: 蜂箱里的蜜蜂正因疾病而相继死亡。

vocabulary.entry: dementia [n.] /dɪˈmenʃə/ 痴呆；痴呆症 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Early diagnosis of dementia can help manage the symptoms.
vocabulary.translation: 痴呆症的早期诊断有助于控制症状。

vocabulary.entry: stretch one's brain [phr.] /stretʃ wʌnz breɪn/ 锻炼大脑 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Doing puzzles is a good way to stretch your brain.
vocabulary.translation: 做谜题是锻炼大脑的好方法。

vocabulary.example: She solves the crossword in the newspaper every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天早上都会解报纸上的填字游戏。

vocabulary.example: Sudoku is a popular number puzzle that tests logic.
vocabulary.translation: 数独是一种流行的测试逻辑的数字谜题。

vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can boost your energy levels.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼可以提高你的能量水平。

vocabulary.example: Solving complex problems requires a lot of brainpower.
vocabulary.translation: 解决复杂问题需要大量的脑力。

vocabulary.entry: neuropsychologist [n.] /ˌnjʊərəʊsaɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ 神经心理学家 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The neuropsychologist assessed the patient's cognitive function.
vocabulary.translation: 神经心理学家评估了患者的认知功能。

vocabulary.example: Being bilingual has many cognitive benefits.
vocabulary.translation: 会双语有很多认知方面的好处。

vocabulary.example: He suffered a stroke that left him unable to speak.
vocabulary.translation: 他患了中风，导致无法说话。

vocabulary.example: Reading stimulates the imagination.
vocabulary.translation: 阅读能激发想象力。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive reserve [n.] /ˈkɒɡnətɪv rɪˈzɜːv/ 认知储备 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Education helps build cognitive reserve against dementia.
vocabulary.translation: 教育有助于建立抵御痴呆症的认知储备。

vocabulary.entry: put one's mind at rest [phr.] /pʊt wʌnz maɪnd æt rest/ 使安心 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The doctor's reassurance put my mind at rest.
vocabulary.translation: 医生的安慰让我安心了。

vocabulary.example: The new software enhances productivity.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件提高了生产力。

vocabulary.example: She acquired a good knowledge of French.
vocabulary.translation: 她学到了很好的法语知识。

vocabulary.entry: utilise [v.] /ˈjuːtəlaɪz/ 利用 (英式拼写，美式: utilize；书面语)
vocabulary.example: We need to utilise our resources more efficiently.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要更有效地利用资源。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive performance [n.] /ˈkɒɡnətɪv pəˈfɔːməns/ 认知表现 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Sleep is essential for optimal cognitive performance.
vocabulary.translation: 睡眠对于最佳的认知表现至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: brain box [n.] /breɪn bɒks/ 聪明人 (英式英语；口语)
vocabulary.example: He's a real brain box – he knows the answer to everything.
vocabulary.translation: 他真是个聪明人——什么问题的答案他都知道。

sentences.chinese: 通过学习提高记忆力或智力的方法来训练我们的大脑是个好主意。

sentences.english: I like to stretch my brain by doing a crossword or a Sudoku puzzle.
sentences.chinese: 我喜欢通过做填字游戏或九宫格谜题来锻炼我的大脑。

sentences.english: There's also evidence that learning a second language can boost your brainpower.
sentences.chinese: 也有证据表明，学习第二语言可以增强你的脑力。

sentences.chinese: 神经心理学家凯瑟琳·洛夫迪博士认为，成为双语者可以保护大脑，因为“这涉及到大量的转换，这似乎能锻炼我们大脑的执行区域。

sentences.chinese: 当涉及到抵御中风所带来的某种损害时，大脑的这些部分会更强壮、更健康。”

sentences.english: She says "even if people take up languages or take up other things later in life it will give them a degree of protection."
sentences.chinese: 她说：“即使人们在晚年才开始学习语言或其他事情，这也会给他们一定程度的保护。”

sentences.english: As I get older, that has put my mind at rest!
sentences.chinese: 随着我年龄的增长，这让我安心了不少！

sentences.chinese: 我读过的最棒的研究是，吃巧克力可能会提高我们获取和运用知识的能力——也就是我们的认知表现。

sentences.chinese: 这对我身体的其他部分可能不健康，但至少它可能会让我成为一个聪明人！
